title: 可持久化平衡树与模拟退火
summary: Keep every version of a balanced tree by copying nodes in split and merge, and search hard optimisation problems with simulated annealing plus a final hill climb.

boxes.text: A persistent balanced tree (可持久化平衡树) keeps every version of a set or sequence. FHQ Treap (拓展篇第4章) is the easy one to make persistent: split and merge only touch nodes on a root path, so copy each node before changing it. Every operation then creates O(log n) new nodes and a new root, and old roots still describe old versions (P3835).

Treap priorities are random and never change, so a copied node keeps its priority and the expected shape is unchanged. The sequence version with lazy reversal (P5055) must also copy children when pushing a tag down, because the children may be shared with other versions.

Each line "v op x" works on version v and creates version i. Random operations on random old versions, checked against keeping a separate sorted list for every version in Python. A query creates copies too, but they are thrown away because the version keeps the old root.
Memory: every operation copies O(log n) nodes, so size the pool for (operations × about 50) nodes. Never modify a node that may belong to another version; always copy first (split does it here).
Simulated annealing (模拟退火): a randomised search for the minimum of a messy function. Keep a current point and a temperature T. Each step moves to a random nearby point (step size proportional to T).

It has no guarantee: use it for partial scores or when nothing exact is known, and run it several times from random starts within the time limit. Hill climbing is the T = 0 version (accept only improvements, shrink the step): exact when the function is convex, as in 平衡点(P1337), the weighted point minimising Σ wi·distance.

The weighted geometric median of 8 random points, checked against Weiszfeld's iteration (an exact convergent method) in Python. The final hill-climbing phase with halving steps polishes the annealing result to full precision.

Tune by experiment: starting temperature on the scale of the coordinates, cooling factor 0.99–0.999, and stop by time (clock()) rather than by a fixed count on a real judge. Always keep the best point seen, not just the current one.

title: NOI 与 IOI 专题选讲
en: Chinese postman, misère games, and rare topics
summary: The Chinese postman problem with a bitmask matching, the rule for misère game sums, and a reference table of the rare NOI / IOI topics with one-line ideas.

boxes.text: The Chinese postman problem (中国邮路问题): the shortest closed walk that uses every edge of a connected undirected graph at least once. If every degree is even, the answer is the total weight (an Euler circuit, 拓展篇第17章). Otherwise some edges are walked twice: pair up the odd-degree vertices (there is an even number of them) with the smallest total shortest-path distance, and add that.

Pairing odd vertices = minimum-weight perfect matching on their shortest-path distances. With up to about 20 odd vertices, a bitmask DP matches them (always pair the lowest unmatched vertex); in general it needs weighted blossom. The directed version is a min-cost flow on the in/out-degree imbalance.
Checked against a separate recursive pairing in Python on the same shortest-path distances. Pairing the lowest unpaired vertex first avoids counting each matching many times: O(2ᵏ · k).

Misère and Anti-SG games (Anti-SG / SJ 定理): in "last player to move loses" versions, plain SG fails. For sums of games where a position with SG = 0 everywhere has no move, the first player wins iff either (the SG of the whole sum ≠ 0 and some single game has SG > 1) or (the sum's SG = 0 and no single game has SG > 1). Anti-Nim (拓展篇第10章) is the special case.

Other game patterns that appear at NOI: "every-SG" (players must move in every component, decided by the longest finishing time), games on graphs solved by retrograde analysis (BFS backwards from final positions, counting remaining moves per state), and partisan games where surreal-number values replace SG values (rare).

These are listed so the names are familiar when they appear; each one is a project on its own. The core NOI toolkit is the rest of NOI 篇 : when a problem looks like one of these, first check whether a simpler tool from the earlier chapters already solves it.

Output-only tasks (提交答案题): you get the input files and submit outputs, often scored by quality. There is no time limit, so the strategy is different: look at each input first (many are special: a tree, a path, tiny n), solve the easy ones exactly, then run search or heuristics (simulated annealing 第24章 , random restarts, local search) on the rest for hours on your own machine.

Write a checker that scores your output before trying to improve it, keep the best output of every file, and spend effort where the score gap is largest. Hand-made constructions and visualising the input often beat a general algorithm on special files.

Green Hackenbush on trees (树上删边游戏): a rooted tree; a move deletes an edge, and everything no longer connected to the root disappears; who cannot move loses. Its SG value: SG(u) = XOR over children v of (SG(v) + 1), leaves 0. A chain of length k is a Nim heap of size k, and the "+1" puts the edge above a subtree on top of it like a stalk.

Colon principle: a subtree can be replaced by a chain with the same SG value. For graphs with cycles (fusion principle) an even cycle becomes a single vertex and an odd cycle a vertex with one extra edge, after which the tree rule applies. Sums of several trees: XOR their root values (拓展篇 SG).
The input gives the parent of vertices 2..n. Checked against the full game tree in Python: every set of remaining edges is a state, and its SG value is the mex over all deletions.
